claims.text: CoCrFeMnNi is expected to have a typical FCC microstructure in the initial state.
Mechanical alloying followed by spark plasma sintering is a viable processing route for CoCrFeMnNi.
Approximately 0.5–2 wt% Y2O3 nanoparticles can be incorporated into CoCrFeMnNi by mechanical alloying and spark plasma sintering.
Optimized processing can produce a uniform, non-clustered dispersion of Y2O3 nanoparticles in the CoCrFeMnNi matrix.
Mechanical alloying and spark plasma sintering can produce nanostructured CoCrFeMnNi.
The Y2O3 particles will form a nanoscale dispersion within the FCC matrix.
Dispersed Y2O3 nanoparticles will impede dislocation motion in CoCrFeMnNi.
Dispersed Y2O3 nanoparticles will impede grain-boundary migration and stabilize grain boundaries in CoCrFeMnNi.
Impeded dislocation motion will increase elevated-temperature yield strength.
Grain-boundary stabilization will reduce elevated-temperature creep deformation.
Y2O3-dispersed CoCrFeMnNi will have higher yield strength than identically processed CoCrFeMnNi without nanoparticles.
Y2O3-dispersed CoCrFeMnNi will have improved creep resistance and prolonged creep-rupture life relative to the nanoparticle-free control.
Y2O3-dispersed CoCrFeMnNi will exhibit increased tensile fracture strain relative to the nanoparticle-free control.
The proposed mechanical-property improvements should persist at temperatures up to approximately 900 °C.
The proposed 900 °C test boundary is relevant to extreme-environment applications.
Nonuniform nanoparticle dispersion may reduce or eliminate the predicted improvements.
Non-optimized Y2O3 dispersion may impair ductility.
An identically processed nanoparticle-free CoCrFeMnNi sample provides the control for isolating the effect of Y2O3 addition.
